clue.text: Mark a spy captured in battle

indicators.note: captured means the spy is held inside the letters from mark and a

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A spy is taken prisoner in the middle of a battle, marked down by the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: MAGENTA is a battle of 1859 in northern Italy, which also gave its name to the dye. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta was a battle fought in 1859 between France with Sardinia and Austria.

clue.text: Pole holding binary digits to be revolutionary

indicators.note: holding means the pole contains the digits within it

parts.note: a mast is a tall pole
binary uses only the digits 0 and 1, read as the letters O and I

explanation.surface: A computer pole stuffed with ones and zeros aims to be radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Mao Zedong's Communist doctrine is a revolutionary.

clue.text: Gad! Grand house turned over to one of the workers

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: turned over means the word for house is read backwards

parts.note: a villa is a large country house
worker ants are the labouring caste of an ant colony

explanation.surface: Good heavens! A mansion has been handed over to a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gad!' looks like a mild oath, but it is the verb meaning wander about. 'turned over' gives ALLIV.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about is to roam from place to place in search of pleasure.

clue.text: River's risen about 45 inches? That's not much of a story

indicators.note: about means the reversed river goes round the measure
risen, in a down clue, means the river is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Avon is a river in England
the ell was an old cloth measure of 45 inches

explanation.surface: A river has crept up nearly four feet, but the tale is short.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a flood gauge, but the 45 inches is an old cloth measure. 'That's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a tale longer than a short story but brief.

clue.text: Close to a description of hypotenuse?

definitions.meaning: the hypotenuse is the longest edge of a right-angled triangle

explanation.walkthrough: Split as A LONG SIDE, the second reading describes the hypotenuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside or next to something, as a ship lies against a quay.

clue.text: Blow up again, seeing reason for delay to football match?

definitions.meaning: to inflate a second time; in economics, to expand an economy again

definitions.text: reason for delay to football match?
definitions.meaning: a match cannot start if the referee has not arrived on time

explanation.walkthrough: Split as REF LATE, the second definition is a whimsical explanation of why kick-off was held up. 'seeing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflation is inflating again, whether a tyre or a stalled economy.

clue.text: One emperor upset follower of another

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, means the pair are turned upside down so read backwards

parts.note: one is read as the article a
a tsar was an emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: An emperor overturned the disciple of a rival ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ATSAR backwards. The 'another' emperor is Haile Selassie of Ethiopia, venerated by Rastafarians.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian reveres Haile Selassie, former emperor of Ethiopia, as divine.

clue.text: Nobody is bound to have this

definitions.text: Nobody is bound to have this

parts.words: Nobody is bound to have this
parts.note: reads as a certainty that no one has it, but means it belongs only to someone not tied up

explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' means tied, not certain: only the unbound have this.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty is the condition of not being restrained or tied.

clue.text: Block found to be part of Roman villa

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stone block was found in the ruins of a Roman villa.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Block found to be' as the definition, but only 'Block' can stand for the answer; 'found to be' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith's anvil is a heavy iron block on which metal is hammered.

clue.text: Supporting cast in full costume

definitions.meaning: the group of performers beyond the principals

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is both the company of players and a coordinated outfit.

clue.text: Money I invested in patent for blind

indicators.note: invested in means the money and I are placed inside the word for patent

parts.note: patent as an adjective means plain to see
L stands for pounds (Latin libra), so for money

explanation.surface: Someone sinks cash into a patent for a window blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' looks like a noun (an invention's patent), but it is the adjective meaning evident; 'blind' is not a window covering but means unaware.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blind to something means being unaware of it, heedless.

clue.text: Rock singer succeeded after live broadcast

indicators.note: after says the letter for succeeded goes behind the scrambled word
broadcast in the sense of scattered means the letters of live are spread out anew

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A rock singer took over after a live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock singer' hints at a geologist's joke, but it is simply the King of rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was the leading rock and roll singer of the 1950s.

clue.text: Refuse to drink fast

definitions.meaning: refuse as a noun means kitchen waste, as fed to pigs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb (decline to drink) but is the noun pronounced REF-use. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Swill is waste food given to pigs, and to swill is to gulp liquid greedily.

clue.text: Old woman holding extremely sensational set of titles

indicators.note: holding means the old woman contains the picked letters inside her

parts.note: grandam is an old word for a grandmother or old woman

indicators.note: extremely means take only the extreme letters of the following word

explanation.surface: An elderly lady clings to a thrilling run of championship wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' tempts GRAN, but the longer archaic GRANDAM is needed to hold the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning all the major championships in a sport, such as tennis or golf, in one season is a clean sweep of titles.

clue.text: Such a figure can represent nothing. Roman predecessors didn't

definitions.text: Such a figure can represent nothing. Roman predecessors didn't

parts.words: Such a figure can represent nothing. Roman predecessors didn't
parts.note: the Hindu-Arabic system has a digit for zero, which the Roman system it replaced had no symbol for

explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing' means zero: the figure 0 exists among the digits Europe adopted from the Arabs, while Roman numerals had no zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The digit 0 belongs to the Arabic number system, while Roman numerals lacked any symbol for zero.

clue.text: Taking up an employment, a delinquent was sick

indicators.note: taking up, in a down clue, means lifting a word so it reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: use is employment, as in putting to use
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth often seen as a delinquent

explanation.surface: Having taken on a job, a young offender threw up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking up' reverses AN to NA. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling nauseated means feeling queasy, as though about to vomit.

clue.text: Former character I subsequently put up to return

indicators.note: put up, in a down clue, means the whole run is raised so it reads backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet
later means subsequently

explanation.surface: An ex-character I then nominated for a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses ETAILATER as a whole. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to hit back, returning an injury in kind.

clue.text: Type of art one couldn't put a figure on

definitions.text: Type of art one couldn't put a figure on

parts.words: Type of art one couldn't put a figure on
parts.note: reads as art too valuable to price, but means art containing no human figures, non-representational

explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' means a depicted form, not a price.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-figurative art uses shape and colour rather than depicting recognisable objects.

clue.text: Stoically face dismissal after cut

indicators.note: after says the words for dismissal follow the word for cut

parts.note: a bite, like a cut, is a share of the takings
to get the bullet is slang for being sacked

explanation.surface: Someone takes the sack bravely after a pay cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' means a share, as in 'take a bite of the profits'; 'the bullet' is British slang for dismissal from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something painful with fortitude, as soldiers once bit on a bullet during surgery.

clue.text: Organised workers to look over unknown holiday area

parts.note: TU is a trade union, organised labour
to scan is to look over
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Union members plan to scout an unexplored holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany, in central Italy, is a favourite region for British holidaymakers.

clue.text: Clearly thinking inn's serving American inside

indicators.note: inside places the American within the word for inn

parts.note: a local is a pub near your home, so an inn
GI is a US soldier, hence an American

explanation.surface: A rational pub has an American customer being served.
explanation.walkthrough: THE LOCAL is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub. 'serving' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical reasoning follows clear, coherent steps.

clue.text: Said to get money for a special stamp

indicators.note: said means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to cash a cheque is to get money for it

explanation.surface: Someone is reported to have been paid for a rare postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cash a' said aloud is 'cash-ay', the sound of the French word. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachet is a distinguishing seal or mark, especially one on an envelope.

clue.text: Period property?

parts.note: reads like an old house of a historic style, but means a holiday home owned for a set period each year

explanation.walkthrough: Estate agents' 'period property' is an old building; here it is property you own only for a period.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday flat bought jointly so that each owner may use it for a set number of weeks a year.

clue.text: Just married, before exam

indicators.note: before puts the letter for married ahead of the exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Freshly wed, just ahead of a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only now' but is the adjective meaning fair or righteous.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-minded and fair conduct is ethically sound.

clue.text: A good reduction in spread of yobbery

indicators.note: a reduction in means the word for spread is cut short

parts.note: to grow is to spread or increase

explanation.surface: A welcome fall in the spread of hooliganism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduction in' drops the last letter of GROW. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro, British slang from aggravation, means aggressive troublemaking.

clue.text: Add distinction to a Verdi role

parts.note: to gild is to adorn or lend splendour to something

explanation.surface: A singer brings extra polish to a part in a Verdi opera.
explanation.walkthrough: GILDA is the daughter of the jester in Verdi's opera Rigoletto.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilda is the soprano heroine of Rigoletto, a Verdi opera.

clue.text: Leader of army or reserve force needed carrier of vital supplies

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of army

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: An army commander or reserve unit needs a supply convoy.
explanation.walkthrough: The military picture hides a blood vessel: the 'vital supplies' are oxygenated blood. 'needed' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The main artery carries oxygen-rich blood from the heart to the body.

clue.text: Get a free bash?

parts.note: a bash is a party; turning up to one uninvited gets you in without paying or being asked

explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' is slang for a party, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend a party or event without an invitation, so enjoying it for nothing.

clue.text: Call to pack colleague in ne'ertheless

indicators.note: to pack is to stuff one thing into another
in shows where the colleague is packed, inside the word for ne'ertheless

parts.note: tho is the clipped form of though, meaning nevertheless
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: A summons to cram a co-worker in, regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: Clipped words suit each other: 'ne'ertheless' signals a shortened word, THO. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the huntsman's cry on sighting the fox.

clue.text: Extremely boring time had by US statesman

parts.note: John Foster Dulles was US Secretary of State in the 1950s

explanation.surface: A US politician spent a thoroughly tedious time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had by' is a link phrase: the statesman has T after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of dull, meaning most tedious.
